claims.statement: 未知电流是一种去极化时缓慢失活的钾电流（IKs，E≈-80mV，τ_inact≈200-400ms，hv≈-45mV）。去极化条件脉冲通过失活移除此电流的抑制性影响，导致测试脉冲时放电增强。超极化条件保持该电流完全可用，抑制后续响应。
predicts: depol conditioning + test: 25-45 spikes（K+ 失活移除抑制）
hyperpol conditioning + depol test: 12-25 spikes（K+ 完全可用，抑制测试响应）
long step: 22-35 spikes（部分 K+ 在持续去极化中失活，产生适应）
brief step: 4-10 spikes（太短，K+ 不失活）
claims.note: P16 depol cond + test = 40 spikes 落在 H1 的 support 区间 [35, 60]。H1 定性解释 conditioning 模式：depol conditioning 通过失活移除慢 K+ 抑制导致增强。

claims.statement: 未知效应来自慢 Na 通道失活动力学（slow Na inactivation）：静息时部分 Na 通道处于慢失活态，去极化条件脉冲改变慢失活平衡，影响测试脉冲时可用的 Na 通道数量，从而调制放电响应。
predicts: depol conditioning + test: 22-40 spikes（Na 慢失活改变可用性）
hyperpol conditioning + depol test: 8-20 spikes（超极化影响慢失活平衡）
long step: 20-32 spikes
brief step: 5-12 spikes
claims.note: P16 depol cond + test = 40 spikes，在 H2 预测区间 [22, 40] 的边界上。对抗攻击 G3 指出 H2 预测方向可能错误。H2 标记为 CONTESTED，需要进一步检验。

attacks.text: H0's own <15% criterion is violated: hyperpol conditioning + depol test shows +31.6% deviation from reference model (19.33 vs 14.67). This is a categorical falsification by H0's own stated standard.

Deviation pattern is systematic, not random: simple protocols (long step: 0%, brief step: ~5%) match reference closely, while complex conditioning protocols show large deviations (mean 22.4%, ~9.5x larger). If deviations were pure noise, they should be roughly uniform. Only conditioning-dependent protocols deviate strongly, implying the model misses a conditioning-specific mechanism.

Slow Na inactivation should REDUCE available Na channels after depolarizing conditioning, producing FEWER spikes — yet data show the opposite (depol conditioning → 40 spikes >> hyperpol conditioning → 19.33 spikes). Depolarizing conditioning drives Na channels INTO slow-inactivated state, depleting available pool. The observed pattern is naturally explained instead by a slow depolarization-activated INWARD current (e.g., persistent Na+ or ICAN) that remains active after depolarizing conditioning and BOOSTS excitability. H2 predicts the wrong sign.

IKs simulation yields 36.33 spikes for depol conditioning+test vs real cell's 40.0 — a 9.1% deficit. The largest absolute gap occurs precisely in the condition that is supposed to be the hallmark signature (K+ inactivation removal → enhanced firing), suggesting IKs alone may not fully account for the enhancement. An additional facilitatory process (e.g., ICAN or INaP) may be at work during depol conditioning.

A calcium-activated non-specific cation current (ICAN, E≈-20 to 0mV) provides an equally good account: depol conditioning opens Ca2+ channels → residual intracellular Ca2+ activates ICAN → depolarizing drive during test pulse enhances firing (40 spikes). Hyperpol conditioning minimizes Ca2+ entry → minimal ICAN → less enhancement (19 spikes). This mechanism naturally explains why depol enhancement is larger than what pure K+ inactivation can produce (ICAN is actively facilitatory, not just disinhibitory).

Post-transition attack on SUPPORTED H1: H1 claims slow K+ inactivation (tau 200-400ms) explains depol conditioning enhancement. However, the IKs candidate simulation (g=0.003, E=-80, hvh=-45, htau=400) predicts only 36.33 spikes for depol cond+test, while real cell fires 40 (P16). This 9% deficit suggests IKs alone is insufficient — an additional facilitatory mechanism (e.g., ICAN or INaP) may contribute. H1 is SUPPORTED as the primary mechanism but may be incomplete.

Run-level attack: H1 SUPPORTED by P16 (depol cond+test = 40 in [35,60]). But P12 also measured 40 for the same protocol, and P12 was designed to kill H0, not support H1. The evidence for H1 rests primarily on a single protocol (depol cond+test). The hyperpol cond+test result (19.33, P14) is consistent with H1 but also with other mechanisms. True discrimination requires protocols that differentially engage K+ inactivation vs other candidates (e.g., Ca2+ chelation, varying conditioning duration).
